basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 24.' and it opens 'Vers. 24. Avertitque se parumper et flevit. Jure Joseph | Christum significat, qui tot'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 24. Avertitque se parumper et flevit. Jure Joseph | Christum significat, qui tot virtutibus refulget; castitate, qua amantis dominae improbitatem pro nihilo duxit; sapientia, qua secreta somniorum dissolvebat et futura praedicebat. Erat etiam severus in corrigendis fratribus, pius in fovendis, quorum injurias non solum non ulciscebatur, verum etiam pro illis flebat.
